Note::bool_item¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

bool Note::bool_item() const

Cross From One Bool Lane Into C++ Control Flow¶

bool_item() returns the sole lane of a Bool Note as a native C++ bool. It is the scalar host boundary for a comparison, predicate, or Boolean reduction that has finished its work in Note space. Use it when a result must drive if, while, an assertion, or an API that specifically accepts bool.

The method tests cardinality, not rank. Any defined Bool Note with numel() == 1 is accepted: a rank-zero scalar, shape [1], shape [1, 1], and shape [1, 1, 1] all contain exactly one extractable truth value. is_scalar() is therefore not a prerequisite; it answers the different question of whether the Note has zero axes.

Extraction is constant-time and allocation-free. The native result is copied, so it has no lifetime relationship with the Note. Internally stored Boolean lanes are canonical bytes, and bool_item() maps zero to false and one to true.

No conversion is attempted. A one-element Text, Bytes, Int64, or Float64 Note is rejected rather than interpreted for truthiness. A defined empty Note, a multi-element Bool Note, and an undefined handle are also rejected. Cardinality is validated before dtype, so inputs without exactly one element fail the one-element contract regardless of their dtype.

Keep vectorized decisions as Bool Notes while they are still being combined. Use &, |, ^, ~, all(), and any() first, then call bool_item() once at the final host boundary. Use bools() instead when every lane is needed.

Example 1: Rank Zero And Higher-Rank Singletons¶

const auto scalar = pluss::note::make(false);
const auto rank3 = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<bool>{true}, std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{1, 1, 1});

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "scalar=" << scalar.bool_item()
          << " rank3=" << rank3.bool_item() << '\n';

Output¶

scalar=false rank3=true

The shape [1, 1, 1] remains on rank3; extraction does not reshape it.

Example 2: Finish A Closed-Note Predicate Pipeline¶

const bool found = pluss::note::make("chapter").contains("apt").bool_item();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "pipeline=" << found << '\n';

Output¶

pipeline=true

contains() returns a Bool Note. bool_item() is appropriate here because the scalar text input produces exactly one Boolean result.

Example 3: Empty And Multi-Lane Notes Reject¶

auto report = [](std::string_view label, const pluss::Note& value) {
  try { (void)value.bool_item(); }
  catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << label << ": rejected\n"; }
};

report("bool_item empty", pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{}));
report("bool_item multiple", pluss::note::make({true, false}));

Output¶

bool_item empty: rejected
bool_item multiple: rejected

Do not use bool_item() as an implicit reduction. Choose all() or any() so the aggregation rule is explicit.

Example 4: Numeric One Is Not Boolean True¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::int64_t{1}).bool_item();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "bool_item wrong dtype: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

bool_item wrong dtype: rejected

Example 5: Undefined Has No Lane To Extract¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().bool_item();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "bool_item undefined: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

bool_item undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • bools: borrow every native Boolean lane.

  • is_bool: inspect the dtype without throwing.

  • all: reduce all lanes by conjunction and remain in Note space.

  • any: reduce all lanes by disjunction and remain in Note space.
